Many birds, fish, frogs, and other animals call wetlands their home!

Maraming ibon, isda, palaka, at iba pang hayop ang tumataghan dito!
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang nagpuyo sa mga wetland ug nagsalig sa tubig ug tanom didto?

Daghang langgam, isda, baki, ug uban pang mananap ang nagpuyo didto!

What is a wetland?

A wetland is land that stays wet or covered by shallow water most of the time — like a soggy, watery neighborhood!

Ang wetland o latian ay lupa na halos palaging basa o natatakpan ng mababaw na tubig.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang wetland?

Ang wetland o lamakan usa ka yuta nga halos kanunay basa o gitabunan sa mabaw nga tubig.

What is the biggest fish in the world?

The whale shark is the biggest fish in the world — you can often see one in Donsol or Oslob in the Philippines!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamalaking isda sa mundo?

Ang butanding o whale shark ang pinakamalaking isda sa mundo — madalas itong makita sa Donsol at Oslob sa Pilipinas!
copy.bis:
Unsay kinadak-ang isda sa kalibotan?

Ang butanding o whale shark mao ang kinadak-ang isda sa kalibotan — kasagaran makita kini sa Donsol ug Oslob sa Pilipinas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the butanding is actually a fish — a shark, not a whale!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)

copy.en:
Is a whale shark really a whale?

Nope! Even though it's called a whale shark, the butanding is actually a fish — a shark, not a whale!
copy.tl:
Balyena ba talaga ang whale shark?

Hindi! Kahit tinatawag itong whale shark, ang butanding ay isang isda — pating, hindi balyena!
copy.bis:
Balyena ba gyud ang whale shark?

Dili! Bisan gitawag kini og whale shark, ang butanding usa ka isda — pating, dili balyena!

copy.en:
How long can a whale shark live?

The whale shark can live a very long time — around 70 to 100 years or even more!
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal mabuhay ang butanding?

Ang butanding ay maaaring mabuhay ng napakahabang panahon — mga 70 hanggang 100 taon o higit pa!
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay mabuhi ang butanding?

Ang butanding mahimong mabuhi ug taas kaayo nga panahon — mga 70 ngadto sa 100 ka tuig o sobra pa!

copy.en: The whale shark has beautiful white spots and stripes on its grayish skin.
copy.tl: Ang butanding ay may magagandang puting batik at guhit sa kulay-abong balat nito.
copy.bis: Ang butanding adunay nindot nga puti nga mga tuldok ug guhit sa abuhon nga panit niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: I'd make a great mate
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions mating but does not identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth vs laying eggs. copy.en:
What might a whale's song be saying?

Scientists don't fully understand every whale song yet, but they think it might mean things like "I am here" or "I'd make a great mate"!
copy.tl:
Ano kaya ang ibig sabihin ng kanta ng balyena?

Hindi pa lubos na nauunawaan ng mga siyentista ang bawat kanta ng balyena, pero pinaniniwalaang maaaring ibig sabihin nito ay "narito ako" o "magandang kapareha ako"!
copy.bis:
Unsa kaha ang gipasabot sa kanta sa balyena?

Wala pa hingpit masabtan sa mga siyentista ang matag kanta sa balyena, apan gituohan nga mahimong buot ipasabot niini "ania ko" o "maayo kong kapikas"!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That's why other whales can hear it even from far away in the ocean.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that a whale's song can be heard from far away, which touches on sound transfer, but it does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred in everyday situations. assignedReviews.card_evidence: Very loud — louder than many machines people make!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a source of sound (whale song) and its loudness, but it does not observe or identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, home, or in the local community. copy.en:
How loud can a whale's song be?

Very loud — louder than many machines people make! That's why other whales can hear it even from far away in the ocean.
copy.tl:
Gaano kalakas ang kanta ng balyena?

Napakalakas — mas malakas pa kaysa sa maraming makinang gawa ng tao! Kaya naririnig ito ng ibang balyena kahit napakalayo sila sa dagat.
copy.bis:
Unsa ka kusog ang kanta sa balyena?

Kusog kaayo — mas kusog pa kaysa sa daghang makina nga hinimo sa tawo! Mao nga madungog kini sa ubang balyena bisan layo kaayo sila sa dagat.

Alexander Fleming was a Scottish scientist, from Scotland!

copy.bis:

Si Alexander Fleming usa ka Eskoses, taga-Scotland, nga siyentista!

copy.bis: Ang desyerto mao ang uga kaayo nga dapit nga gamay ra kaayo ang ulan, mao nga pipila ra ka tanom ug hayop ang makapuyo didto.

copy.tl: Ang astronaut ay isang taong sinanay para maglakbay at magtrabaho sa kalawakan, na nakasuot ng space suit para mabuhay sa labas ng Earth!
copy.bis: Ang astronaut usa ka tawo nga gibansay aron mobiyahe ug magtrabaho sa kawanangan, nga nagsul-ob og space suit aron mabuhi sa gawas sa Earth!

copy.tl: Ang satellite ay isang human-made machine na umiikot sa Earth para mangalap o magpadala ng impormasyon, tulad ng phone signals o weather pictures!
copy.bis: Ang satellite usa ka human-made machine nga naglibot sa Earth aron magkuha o magpadala og impormasyon, sama sa phone signals o weather pictures!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A model is a representation that helps us picture and understand them.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how seismic wave data has been used to develop a model for the internal structure and composition of the Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains generally why scientists use models, but does not mention seismic wave data, Earth's internal structure, or composition. It shares only the broad concept of models and provides no direct instructional support for the specific competency.

copy.en:
Why do scientists make models if they can just look at the real thing?

Many things in science are too small, too big, or too far away to see clearly. A model is a representation that helps us picture and understand them.
copy.tl:
Bakit gumagawa pa ang mga scientist ng model kung pwede naman nilang tingnan ang totoong bagay?

Maraming bagay sa science ang napakaliit, napakalaki, o napakalayo para makita nang malinaw. Ang model ay isang representasyon na tumutulong sa atin na mailarawan at maintindihan ang mga ito.
copy.bis:
Nganong maghimo pa man ang mga scientist ug model kung pwede ra man nila tan-awon ang tinuod nga butang?

Daghang butang sa science ang gagmay kaayo, dagko kaayo, o layo kaayo para makita nga klaro. Ang model usa ka representasyon nga makatabang nato nga mahanduraw ug masabtan kini.

copy.en: White light is actually a mix! It is made of all the colors of the spectrum mixed perfectly together.
copy.tl: Ang puting liwanag ay isang halo! Ito ay binubuo ng lahat ng kulay ng spectrum na pinagsama-sama.
copy.bis: Ang puti nga kahayag usa ka sagol! Gilangkuban kini sa tanang kolor sa spectrum nga gisagol nga hingpit.

Who discovered Charon, the largest moon of Pluto?

James Christy! It is known as the largest moon of Pluto.
copy.tl:
Sino ang nakatuklas ng Charon, ang pinakamalaking buwan ng Pluto?

Si James Christy! Ito ang pinakamalaking buwan ng Pluto.
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang nakadiskobre sa Charon, ang pinakadako nga bulan sa Pluto?

Si James Christy! Kini ang pinakadako nga bulan sa Pluto.

Do slow animals ever survive?

Yes! Some slow animals like turtles have a hard shell or tough skin that protects them, so they stay safe even without running fast.
copy.tl:
Kaya bang mabuhay ang mabagal na hayop?

Oo! May mga mabagal na hayop tulad ng pagong na may matigas na bahay o balat na proteksyon, kaya ligtas sila kahit hindi makatakbo.
copy.bis:
Makalahutay ba ang hinay nga mananap?

Oo! Ang uban hinay nga mananap sama sa bao adunay gahi nga panit nga manalipod, mao nga luwas gihapon sila bisan dili makadagan.

Why does bread go hard and stale?

The starch inside changes shape and loses softness, even inside a sealed bag!

Ang almirol sa loob ay nagbabago ng ayos at nawawalan ng lambot kahit nasa supot!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga mogahi ang tinapay?

Ang almirol sa sulod mausab og porma ug mawad-an sa kahumok, bisan sa sulod sa supot!

Ever wonder why chili makes your mouth feel like it's burning?

Chili has capsaicin — a substance that tricks your mouth nerves into feeling burned, even though there's no real heat!
copy.tl:
Bakit parang nasusunog ang bibig mo pagkain ng sili?

May capsaicin ang sili — isang sangkap na niloloko ang mga nerbiyos sa bibig mo na akala'y nasusunog, kahit walang tunay na init!
copy.bis:
Ngano murag nasunog ang imong baba pagkaon og sili?

Ang sili adunay capsaicin — usa ka sustansya nga molimbong sa mga nerbiyos sa baba nga akala nasunog, bisan walay tinuod nga init!

copy.en:
Why do fingers wrinkle in water?

Your nervous system actually does this on purpose — wrinkly fingertips help you grip wet things better, it's not the skin soaking up water!
copy.tl:
Bakit nangungunot ang daliri kapag matagal sa tubig?

Sinasadya ito ng iyong nerbiyos — mas madaling makahawak ng basang bagay kapag kunot ang daliri, hindi ito dahil sumisipsip ng tubig ang balat!
copy.bis:
Ngano mokunot ang tudlo kon dugay sa tubig?

Gituyo kini sa imong nerbiyos — mas sayon makagunit sa basa nga butang kon kunot ang tudlo, dili tungod misuyop og tubig ang panit!

Why does a sharp knife cut better than a dull one?

A sharp knife's thin edge puts all your push onto a tiny area, making very high pressure to slice! A dull knife spreads the force out.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas mahusay humiwa ang matalas na kutsilyo?

Ang manipis na talim nito ay nagpapatong ng buong puwersa mo sa napakaliit na lugar, kaya napakataas ng presyon! Sa mapurol, kumakalat ang puwersa.
copy.bis:
Nganong mas maayong mohiwa ang hait nga kutsilyo?

Ang nipis nga sulab niini magbutang sa tibuok nimong kusog sa gamay kaayong dapit, maong taas kaayo ang presyon! Sa habol, magkatag ang kusog.

Why does milk left out of the fridge turn sour and lumpy?

Bacteria grow in it, eating the milk's sugar and making acid!

Bakit naaasim at kumakapal ang gatas na iniwan sa labas ng ref?

Dumarami ang bakterya rito, kumakain ng asukal sa gatas at gumagawa ng acid!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga moaslom ug molapot ang gatas nga gibilin gawas sa ref?

Modaghan ang bakterya niini, mokaon sa kalamay sa gatas ug mobuhat og acid!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Warm, moist cooked rice left out is a favorite place for bacteria to grow
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about food spoilage and bacterial growth, not about identifying the basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: so keep it in the fridge to last longer
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: Refrigeration to slow spoilage touches food preservation, but the card does not explain factors affecting rates of chemical reactions, such as temperature, concentration, or surface area, nor does it connect spoilage to chemical reaction rates.

copy.en: Warm, moist cooked rice left out is a favorite place for bacteria to grow, so keep it in the fridge to last longer!
copy.tl: Ang mainit at basang kanin na iniwan sa labas ay paboritong tubuan ng bakterya, kaya ilagay sa ref para tumagal!
copy.bis: Ang init ug basa nga kan-on nga gibilin sa gawas paborito nga tuboan sa bakterya, mao nga ibutang sa ref aron mas dugay!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your skin is building new cells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that cells reproduce through two types of cell division, mitosis and meiosis, and describe mitosis as cell division for growth and repair
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that skin builds new cells, which is a result of mitosis, but it does not teach cell division, mitosis, or meiosis, nor does it describe mitosis as growth and repair. The focus is on why a scab itches, not on cellular reproduction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the nerves underneath get stirred up
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses skin and nerves, but the competency covers muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory systems. Skin and nerve sensation are not among these systems, and the card does not describe any of the listed body systems.

copy.en:
Why does a healing scab itch?

Your skin is building new cells and the nerves underneath get stirred up — that's why it itches! Better not to scratch, so it doesn't reopen.
copy.tl:
Bakit kumakati ang gumagaling na sugat?

Bumubuo ang balat ng bagong selula at naiistimula ang nerbiyo sa ilalim ng langib — kaya makati! Huwag kamutin para hindi mabuksan ulit.
copy.bis:
Ngano makatol ang naayo nga samad?

Naghimo ang panit og bag-ong selula ug nasamok ang nerbiyo ilalom sa langib — mao nga makatol! Ayaw kamuta aron dili mabuka pag-usab.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: blue light from the sun scatters more off tiny particles in the air than other colors do
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the relative wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves, including radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultra-violet, x-rays, and gamma radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why the sky appears blue due to scattering of blue light, but does not compare the relative wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves as required by the competency. It mentions only visible light (blue) and does not address radio waves, microwaves, infrared, ultraviolet, x-rays, or gamma radiation, nor their wavelength/frequency relationships.

copy.en: The sky is blue because blue light from the sun scatters more off tiny particles in the air than other colors do!
copy.tl: Asul ang langit dahil ang asul na liwanag mula sa araw ay mas madaling kumalat sa mga particle ng hangin kaysa sa ibang kulay!
copy.bis: Asul ang langit tungod kay ang asul nga kahayag gikan sa adlaw mas dali nga mokatag sa gagmay nga partikulo sa hangin kaysa sa ubang kolor!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Knowing an insect's life cycle helps us control pests
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions insect life cycles but does not use flow charts or compare different stages of any animal life cycle. It only states that knowing life cycles helps control pests, which is not the specific skill of comparing stages via flow charts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: removing stagnant water so mosquitoes can't grow there
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that there is a need to protect and conserve the environment for living things to survive
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about controlling pests by removing stagnant water, not about protecting or conserving the environment for living things to survive. It does not address the need for conservation or protection of habitats.

copy.en:
Why do scientists study insect life cycles?

Knowing an insect's life cycle helps us control pests — like removing stagnant water so mosquitoes can't grow there.
copy.tl:
Bakit inaaral ang siklo ng buhay ng insekto?

Ang pag-alam sa siklo ng buhay ng insekto ay tumutulong na kontrolin ang mga peste, gaya ng pag-aalis ng nakatigil na tubig para sa lamok.
copy.bis:
Nganong gitun-an ang siklo sa kinabuhi sa insekto?

Ang pagkahibalo sa siklo sa kinabuhi sa insekto motabang sa pagpugong sa mga peste, sama sa pagkuha sa nagtigib nga tubig batok sa lamok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Every pattern is unique — even identical twins have different fingerprints!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of DNA, genes, and chromosomes in the transmission of traits
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that fingerprints are unique traits but does not explain the role of DNA, genes, or chromosomes in transmitting traits. It provides no instruction on genetic transmission, so it only shares the same broad topic of inherited traits.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fingerprints are tiny ridges that help us grip things and feel textures.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses fingerprints, which belong to the integumentary system, not any of the listed body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory). It does not describe how any of those systems work.

copy.en:
Why does everyone have different fingerprints?

Fingerprints are tiny ridges that help us grip things and feel textures. Every pattern is unique — even identical twins have different fingerprints!
copy.tl:
Bakit iba-iba ang fingerprint ng bawat tao?

Ang fingerprint ay maliliit na guhit na tumutulong sa paghawak ng bagay at pagdama ng texture. Natatangi ang pattern ng bawat isa — magkaiba pa rin kahit kambal!
copy.bis:
Nganong lahi-lahi ang fingerprint sa matag tawo?

Ang fingerprint mao ang gagmayng linya nga makatabang sa pagkupot og butang ug pagbati sa texture. Talagsaon ang pattern sa matag usa — lahi gihapon bisan kambal!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tiny particles drift off objects and spread through the air via diffusion until they reach our nose!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card illustrates that particles move and spread (diffusion), which is a prerequisite example of particle motion, but it does not describe the full set of particle model properties (constant motion, spaces, attraction, and temperature dependence) required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tiny particles drift off objects and spread through the air via diffusion until they reach our nose!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions particles in air but does not describe the shape and volume properties of solids, liquids, or gases, which is the focus of the competency.

copy.en:
How do we smell things?

Tiny particles drift off objects and spread through the air via diffusion until they reach our nose! That's why you smell cooking food from another room.
copy.tl:
Paano tayo nakakaamoy?

May napakaliliit na particle na pumupulas sa bagay at kumakalat sa hangin (diffusion) hanggang sa ilong natin! Kaya naaamoy mo ang ulam kahit nasa kabilang silid ka.
copy.bis:
Unsaon nato pagsimhot?

Adunay gagmayng partikulo nga mobuhi gikan sa butang ug mokatag sa hangin (diffusion) hangtod sa atong ilong! Mao nga masimhot nimo ang sud-an bisan lain og kwarto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wild greens help many Filipino families stretch a meal for free
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses using wild greens as food to stretch a meal, but it does not teach the concept of basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It only incidentally mentions food as a need without identifying or explaining basic needs.

copy.en: Wild greens help many Filipino families stretch a meal for free — added to soup, sauteed, or mixed with rice to fill up even when money is tight.
copy.tl: Nakakatulong ang gulay-ligaw sa maraming pamilyang Pilipino na dagdagan ang pagkain nang walang gastos — maisasabaw, maigigisa, o maihahalo sa kanin para mabusog kahit kaunti ang pera.
copy.bis: Nakatabang ang gulay-ligaw sa daghang pamilyang Pilipino sa pagdugang sa pagkaon nga walay gasto — maisabaw, maigisa, o maisagol sa kan-on aron mabusog bisan gamay ang kwarta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dust devils are small spinning columns of air over hot, dry ground in summer
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and record changes in the weather during a day or over some days and describe the different types and patterns of weather in the local area
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific weather-related phenomenon (dust devils) but does not teach observing/recording weather changes or describing types/patterns of weather in the local area. It is a factual description, not an activity or pattern explanation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dust devils are small spinning columns of air over hot, dry ground in summer
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a wind phenomenon but does not identify basic weather characteristics such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, or cloud cover. It does not directly support the competency's focus on weather descriptors.

copy.en: Dust devils are small spinning columns of air over hot, dry ground in summer — much smaller and weaker than tornadoes!
copy.tl: Ang mga dust devil ay maliliit na umiikot na hangin sa mainit at tuyong lupa sa tag-init — mas maliit at mahina kaysa tornado!
copy.bis: Ang mga dust devil gagmay nga nagikot nga hangin ibabaw sa mainit ug mamala nga yuta sa tag-init — mas gamay ug mahina kaysa mga tornado!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Scientists read these as wind erosion clues!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes wind sculpting a rock into a ventifact, which is about erosion shaping a rock, not about demonstrating how erosion transports Earth materials. It does not address transport of materials.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Meet the ventifact—a rock sculpted by wind and sand!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a rock and its wind-carved feature, but it does not involve exploring the school grounds or local area, collecting different rocks, or comparing texture, color, or grain crystal size as required by the competency.

copy.en: Meet the ventifact—a rock sculpted by wind and sand! Wind blowing from one direction smooths one side into a flat face. Scientists read these as wind erosion clues!
copy.tl: Kilalanin ang ventifact—isang batong hinubog ng hangin at buhangin! Ang hangin mula sa isang direksyon ay pinapakinis ang isang panig. Binabasa ito ng mga siyentista bilang bakas ng wind erosion!
copy.bis: Ilha ang ventifact—bato nga gihubog sa hangin ug balas! Ang hangin gikan sa usa ka direksyon mopahapsay sa usa ka kilid. Gibasa kini sa mga siyentista isip timailhan sa wind erosion!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the tip of a long blade can move faster than a car on the highway — it travels a huge distance with every rotation!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions speed and distance traveled per rotation, but it does not define speed as distance per unit time or explicitly connect distance and time. It only states that the tip moves fast, which is related to the concept of speed but does not directly teach the competency's core idea.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the tip of a long blade can move faster than a car on the highway — it travels a huge distance with every rotation!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses blade tip speed, not factors affecting the movement of objects such as size, shape, heaviness, material, or surface texture. There is no mention of these factors, so it does not support this competency.

copy.en:
How fast do wind turbine blade tips really move?

Even though big wind turbines look like they turn slowly, the tip of a long blade can move faster than a car on the highway — it travels a huge distance with every rotation!
copy.tl:
Gaano kabilis talaga ang dulo ng pako ng wind turbine?

Kahit mukhang mabagal umikot ang malalaking wind turbine, ang dulo ng mahabang pako ay maaaring kumilos nang mas mabilis pa sa kotse sa highway — malayo ang nilalakbay nito sa bawat pag-ikot!
copy.bis:
Unsa ka paspas gyud ang tumoy sa pako sa wind turbine?

Bisan og morag hinay motuyok ang dagkong wind turbine, ang tumoy sa taas nga pako mahimong molihok nga mas paspas pa sa sakyanan sa highway — layo kaayo ang gibiyahe niini matag tuyok!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That is why they make lift even while hovering in one spot.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe everyday situations that demonstrate: a. balanced forces such as a box resting on an inclined plane, a man standing still, or an object moving with constant velocity; b. unbalanced forces, such as freely falling fruit or an accelerating car
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions lift (a force) but does not identify or describe balanced or unbalanced forces, nor any everyday situation demonstrating them. It is only tangentially about forces.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A helicopter's spinning blades act just like rotating wings!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out simple investigations to demonstrate that contact forces cause objects to move in the same direction as the direction that the force is applied
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses lift from spinning blades but does not demonstrate contact forces causing motion in the direction of the applied force. It is not about contact forces or direction of motion.

copy.en: A helicopter's spinning blades act just like rotating wings! That is why they make lift even while hovering in one spot.
copy.tl: Ang umiikot na blades ng helikopter ay parang mga pakpak na umiikot! Kaya nakakagawa ito ng lift kahit nakatigil sa isang lugar.
copy.bis: Ang nagtuyok nga blades sa helikopter sama sa nagtuyok nga mga pako! Busa makahimo kini og lift bisan naglutaw sa usa ka dapit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The engines give thrust to move the plane forward!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out simple investigations to demonstrate that contact forces cause objects to move in the same direction as the direction that the force is applied
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an example of thrust moving a plane forward, but it does not mention contact forces, direction of force relative to motion, or any simple investigation. It shares vocabulary about forces and motion but does not directly support the competency's required skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The engines give thrust to move the plane forward!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces act between objects and can be measured
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes thrust as a force that moves the plane, but it does not address forces acting between objects or how forces can be measured. It is only a general example of a force causing motion, not direct instruction for this competency.

copy.en: The engines give thrust to move the plane forward! This makes air flow over the wings to create lift.
copy.tl: Ang makina ang nagbibigay ng thrust para umusad ang eroplano! Kaya dumadaloy ang hangin sa pakpak para magka-lift.
copy.bis: Ang makina ang naghatag og thrust aron mo-uswag ang eroplano! Busa modagayday ang hangin sa pako aron magka-lift.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They're the very last molars to grow
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states when wisdom teeth erupt. It does not describe how any of the listed body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work. Teeth are not one of the named systems, and no system function is explained.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: usually appearing during the teenage years or once you're an adult
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a stage of human development (teenage/adult) but does not compare life cycles of mammals, birds, or plants. It provides no information about birth, egg, seed, or maturation stages, so it does not support the competency's comparison task.

copy.en:
When do wisdom teeth usually grow in?

They're the very last molars to grow — usually appearing during the teenage years or once you're an adult.
copy.tl:
Kailan karaniwang tumutubo ang wisdom teeth?

Ito ang pinakahuling bagang na tumutubo — karaniwan nang lumalabas kapag tinedyer na o matanda na.
copy.bis:
Kanus-a kasagaran motubo ang wisdom teeth?

Kini ang kataposan nga bag-ang nga motubo — kasagaran mogawas sa pagkatin-edyer o pagkahamtong na.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It floats because it is less dense than water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains density, a property of matter, but does not describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. It does not directly support the competency's definition of matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It floats because it is less dense than water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses density, which is a physical property, but the competency specifically lists examples like hard, shiny, or stretchable. Density is not among the listed properties and the card does not describe solid materials in those terms.

copy.en:
Why does most wood float on water?

It floats because it is less dense than water!
copy.tl:
Bakit lumulutang ang karamihan ng wood sa tubig?

Lumulutang ito dahil ito ay less dense kaysa tubig!
copy.bis:
Nganong molutaw ang kasagaran sa wood sa tubig?

Molutaw kini kay kini less dense kay sa tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A woodpecker has tiny feathers covering its nostrils that block wood dust while it drills into trees.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (nostril feathers) and its function (blocking wood dust), but the competency specifically requires identifying the role of outer body parts to move and to gather food. The function here is neither movement nor food gathering, so it does not directly support the stated skill.

copy.en: A woodpecker has tiny feathers covering its nostrils that block wood dust while it drills into trees.
copy.tl: May maliliit na balahibo sa butas ng ilong ng woodpecker na humaharang sa alikabok ng kahoy habang ito ay humuhukay.
copy.bis: Ang woodpecker adunay gagmay nga balhibo sa buho sa ilong nga nagsagang sa abog sa kahoy samtang mokalot kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wool usually comes from sheep, but we can also get it from other thick-coated animals like goats for cashmere and alpacas!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some useful things that people have made from non-living materials and describe what natural materials have been used to make the items
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about useful things made from non-living materials (earth materials). Wool is an animal product, a living material, so the card does not support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wool usually comes from sheep, but we can also get it from other thick-coated animals like goats for cashmere and alpacas!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions animals and their thick coats, but the competency is about observing and describing outer body parts (head, legs, wings) and their roles in movement and food gathering. The card does not describe body parts or their functions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wool usually comes from sheep, but we can also get it from other thick-coated animals like goats for cashmere and alpacas!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about animals changing to better suit their environment (e.g., mimicry, camouflage). The card mentions thick coats but does not explain adaptation or environmental change, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Wool usually comes from sheep, but we can also get it from other thick-coated animals like goats for cashmere and alpacas!
copy.tl: Karaniwang galing sa tupa ang wool, pero pwede rin itong galing sa ibang makakapal na balahibong hayop tulad ng kambing (cashmere) at alpaca!
copy.bis: Kasagaran ang wool gikan sa karnero, pero pwede sad kini gikan sa ubang hayop nga baga ang balahibo, sama sa kanding (cashmere) ug alpaca!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When work is done, energy is transferred from one object to another!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that work is done when a force causes the displacement of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that work transfers energy, but the competency requires recognizing that work is done when a force causes displacement. The card does not mention force or displacement, so it does not directly support the competency's core concept.

copy.en: When work is done, energy is transferred from one object to another!
copy.tl: Kapag may nagagawang trabaho, may enerhiyang inililipat mula sa isang bagay patungo sa iba!
copy.bis: Kung naa'y trabaho nga nahimo, naa'y enerhiya nga gibalhin gikan sa usa ka butang ngadto sa lain!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A worker ant's two antennae work like its nose and hands — it uses them to smell, touch, and even 'talk' to other ants!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes antennae as an outer body part and their role in sensing and communication, but the competency specifically requires identifying the role of outer body parts to move and to gather food. Antennae are not presented as aiding movement or food gathering, so the card does not directly support the stated skill.

copy.en:
What are an ant's antennae for?

A worker ant's two antennae work like its nose and hands — it uses them to smell, touch, and even 'talk' to other ants!
copy.tl:
Para saan ang antennae ng langgam?

Ang dalawang antennae ng worker ant ay parang ilong at kamay nito — ginagamit niya ito para umamoy, makakapa, at makausap ang ibang langgam!
copy.bis:
Para unsa ang antennae sa langgam?

Ang duha ka antennae sa worker ant sama sa ilong ug kamot niini — gamiton niya kini aron makapanimaho, makahikap, ug makig-istorya sa ubang langgam!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Worker ants and worker bees are alike in many ways
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card compares worker ants and worker bees but does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups (mammals, reptiles, insects, etc.). It only mentions two insect examples and does not support the classification skill required by G5-L-4.

copy.en: Worker ants and worker bees are alike in many ways — both are female, both work for their queen, and both live in a colony. Bees just fly and make honey too.
copy.tl: Magkatulad sa maraming paraan ang worker ant at worker bee — parehong babae, parehong nagtatrabaho para sa reyna, at parehong nakatira sa kolonya. Ang bubuyog lang ang lumilipad at gumagawa ng pulot.
copy.bis: Managsama sa daghang paagi ang worker ant ug worker bee — parehong babaye, parehong nagtrabaho para sa reyna, ug parehong nagpuyo sa kolonya. Ang putyukan ra ang molupad ug mohimo og dugos.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: dangerous white bristles that break off and stick into skin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (bristles) but its role is defense/irritation, not movement or gathering food as required by G3-L-4.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's common on Philippine reefs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a list or draw up a table with examples of animals and plants in a particular habitat, such as a garden, rice field, seashore, and mangrove swamp
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a Philippine reef habitat but does not make a list or table of animals and plants in a named habitat, and the format-required list/table is absent.

copy.en: The fireworm is a bristly sea worm with dangerous white bristles that break off and stick into skin — touching it causes painful stinging and swelling. It's common on Philippine reefs.
copy.tl: Ang fireworm ay isang mabuhok na dagat-uod na may mapanganib na puting bristle na madaling humihiwalay at tumatagos sa balat — nagdudulot ng masakit na pangangati at pamamaga kapag nahawakan. Karaniwan ito sa mga bahurang Pilipino.
copy.bis: Ang fireworm usa ka mabungol nga dagat nga uod nga adunay peligrosong puting bristle nga dali mahilis ug mosulod sa panit — nagpahinabo og masakit nga pangangati ug pamaga kon hikapon. Komon kini sa mga bahura sa Pilipinas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: People with diabetes or older people heal more slowly because their blood flow is weaker
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Slower healing from weaker blood flow is a disease condition, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: their blood flow is weaker, so wounds need extra care
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Diabetes healing is not the five body systems as a set.

copy.en:
Why do some wounds heal more slowly?

Not everyone heals at the same speed. People with diabetes or older people heal more slowly because their blood flow is weaker, so wounds need extra care.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas mabagal gumaling ang ilang sugat?

Hindi pare-pareho ang bilis ng paggaling ng tao. Sa may diabetes o matatanda, mas mabagal gumaling ang sugat dahil mas mahina ang daloy ng dugo, kaya kailangan itong alagaang mabuti.
copy.bis:
Nganong mas hinay mo-ayo ang pipila ka samad?

Dili managsama ang katulin sa pag-ayo sa mga tawo. Sa adunay diabetes o sa tigulang, mas hinay mo-ayo ang samad kay mas huyang ang dagan sa dugo, busa kinahanglan atimanon pag-ayo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: less skin needs rebuilding — fewer cells and less time needed!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that cells reproduce through two types of cell division, mitosis and meiosis, and describe mitosis as cell division for growth and repair
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why shallow scrapes heal faster (fewer cells to rebuild), but it does not teach cell division types (mitosis/meiosis) or describe mitosis as the mechanism for growth and repair. The healing concept is only tangentially related to the competency's focus on cellular reproduction.

copy.en:
Why do small scrapes heal faster than deep cuts?

A shallow scrape heals faster than a deep cut because less skin needs rebuilding — fewer cells and less time needed!

Bakit mas mabilis gumaling ang gasgas kaysa malalim na sugat?

Mas mabilis gumaling ang mababaw na gasgas kaysa malalim na sugat dahil mas kaunting balat ang kailangang itayong muli — mas kaunting selula at oras lang!

Nganong paspas mo-ayo ang gasgas kaysa lawom nga samad?

Mas paspas mo-ayo ang mabaw nga gasgas kaysa lawom nga samad kay gamay ra nga panit ang kinahanglan tukoron pag-usab — gamay ra nga selula ug panahon!
